lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A military radar scope tracked an unknown target over England at up to four thousand miles per hour.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: August thirteenth, nineteen fifty-six. A C-Forty-Seven pilot and ground observers saw a fast white light.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: At Lakenheath, golf-ball-sized lights shrank to pinpoints.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The Royal Air Force sent a Venom fighter to intercept.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: But watch supervisor Forrest Perkins wrote that the target whipped behind the fighter and shadowed it for ten minutes.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: He said the frightened pilot tried everything to shake it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A classified teleprinter message three days later broadly agreed.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Yet the Venom crews later told researchers they saw only a stationary blip, and no chase.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Skeptics blamed Perseid meteors and false echoes. The Condon Report called a genuine unknown fairly probable.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: So did false returns fool the watch room, or did something outfly a jet on that military radar scope?
